doc.title: Pete Barbutti interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 8, 2022

title: Turning down the Penn State scholarship
summary: He chose the road with a band over a music scholarship, having played percussion with the Philharmonic and local bands; parents supportive.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: School days: grades, teachers and leaving school

blocks.x: The question that’s been rattling around in my head since I knew we were going to meet, when you were getting ready to graduate from high school is it true that you turned down a music scholarship to Penn State?

Yeah. You know I had the chance to go on the road with a band and that to me was infinitely more exciting. Although I loved classical music, you know I was doing a lot, in fact I was playing with the Philharmonic when I was in high school. A percussionist. And

I was playing with the University of Scranton band and I was playing with what they call the Demolay Band and the Shriner band, and then there was another fine orchestra in town called the Cetta Parish band. And I was doing all of those playing percussion.
Did your parents question your choice to not take that scholarship?

No. No. They were supportive of just about anything I wanted to do. I’m not sure it was the right or wrong choice or whatever, you know it doesn’t matter as you look back. But I think sometimes maybe it would have been fun to do that but then again I don’t know.
